reasons: All 8 derived task claims are proven: the recipe asserts the declared and resolved controller version, gates on a clean full-repo tsc, gates on 8 targeted Jest suites, and drives five real Mobile Perps flows (market order with TP/SL, limit order, position Auto close, position close, full open/close lifecycle) with controller-state assertions after each UI gesture.

The recipe has a genuine removal test: reverting any of the six widened OrderType signatures, the toast-bucket resolution, or the 14 PerpsErrorCode entries reintroduces the 19 TypeScript errors that assert-typecheck-clean asserts are gone, so the recipe fails without the change.

Warn rather than pass because the recipe is flaky against live HyperLiquid testnet: of five runs, three passed 207/207 and two failed in different library-flow assertions (prove-market-order/restore-market teardown racing the just-placed TP/SL triggers; prove-limit-order/assert-open-order when the limit order filled instead of resting).
Neither flake implicates the change under test, and both live in called library recipes rather than the authored nodes, but a proof a reviewer cannot re-run green on demand is not a pass-grade proof.
Screenshot evidence is orientation-only by design: this change has no user-visible surface, so the binding proof for every claim is compiler, test-runner, or controller state rather than pixels.
better_version_guidance: Make prove-limit-order deterministic by resting the order far from the touch (a percentage offset from mid) instead of the live Bid preset, so it cannot fill during the proof window.
Give the library teardown a bounded retry or settle window before asserting no open orders, so a just-filled parent's TP/SL triggers cannot race the assertion.

Consider asserting the two new v11-visible signals directly — Order.orderType reporting 'market' for a stop-market trigger, and Position.takeProfitOrders / stopLossOrders — which would turn the incidental observation made during run 2 into a standing regression guard.

coverage.reason: All 8 derived task claims proven; no weak or missing rows.

graphQuality.reason: Cheap state asserts gate first, then the compile and test gates, then five real UI flows; every node carries an intent and the graph terminates in a single end node.

evidenceFit.reason: Compiler and test evidence for the type-level claims, controller state plus read-and-verified screenshots for the UI flows. The order-result frame shows the 'Order submitted' toast emitted by the exact expression this change introduces. Market-order screenshots are overwritten by the limit-order flow (same library filenames), so that claim is graded state-only rather than dressed up with a screenshot that shows a different run.

flakeRisk.reason: Two of five runs failed in different live-testnet library assertions (teardown order race; limit order filling instead of resting); the other three passed 207/207.
